rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Rough-cut drafts for articles.
Verbatim-frame-cite in reference artefact.
Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
The `**What happened:**` block is OPTIONAL, default is to omit it.
A rule set reconstructed at session start goes stale inside the session — re-derive it per target, not per sweep.
One doc per scarce-attention audience; delta-only.
Trainer-facing text is self-contained.
Business-audience word ban (Agents 101 default).
Memory vs context — use deliberately.
Trust Claude's defaults for structure.
Q1/Q2/Q3 retro interview is banned at every module. Compound-shape varies per module.
Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
Simulation personas never alone.
Student moves stay in conversation with agent.
Specify which CLAUDE.md layer — every time.
Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.
Inline links use target's title, never filename.
Disambiguate shared-word collisions with Claude Code primitives on first student-authored use.
No meta-ask when student has already decided.
`.md` is default file type for student artifacts across curriculum.
Body "read it" / "look at it" / "notice X" after chat-print = dead weight.
Operational reminders live at moment of use, not only where introduced.
Name the artifact, not the act.
Name the outcome; don't walk a professional through trivial mechanics.
Four sharing strategies (Agents 101 M7 canonical) — use verbatim.
Agents 101 M2+ Debrief — canonical shape.
Trust the prompt over the scaffold.
Strategic themes recur in Key Concepts.
Key Concepts shape — theme breadcrumbs, not standalone section.
What You'll Learn shape — capability register, not syllabus.
Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
